# CBDB-Desktop: Status and Texts form revisions, 2026-10-16

Found while writing the Status and Texts sections of the user's guide, not from an automated-testing report, so these entries have no CBDB-D numbers yet. Assign numbers as needed. Changes are in Code/status_form_backend.go, Code/texts_form_backend.go, the two forms' index.html files, Templates/pickers/texts_picker.html and cbdb_styles.css. All changes were compiled and tested.

## Summary

| STA-1 | Export Query Results did not include the index address ID | PlaceID added to StatusRecord and PeopleRecord, selected in both queries and written in both export files | Compiled, tested |
| STA-2 | Include sub-units and Use XY were available with no place selected, and stayed ticked after All Places | Checkboxes disabled until a place is selected; All Places unticks and disables them; labels greyed while disabled | Tested |

## STA-1: Index address ID in Export Query Results

**Change.** Both result types now carry the person's index address ID, so the exported files can be joined to ADDR_CODES without a further lookup.

- StatusRecord and PeopleRecord have a new field, PlaceID \*int (JSON placeId). It is a pointer, so a person with no index address comes through as null and exports as a blank, not 0.
- Both queries in handleQueryStatus select bm.c_index_addr_id AS place_id, and both Scan calls read it into PlaceID. Adding the column does not change the SELECT DISTINCT results, because the index address depends only on the person.
- StatusRecords.tsv has a new PlaceID column after IndexYear; StatusRecordsPeople.tsv has one after Sex. Both are written with statusNullIntStr.

**Not affected.** The Status and People tabs do not display the new field. The GIS (tab and KML) export does not write it. The Neo4j export already looked up index addresses itself and is unchanged.

**For the user's guide.** PlaceID is the person's index address (BIOG_MAIN.c_index_addr_id), the same place shown in the Place columns.

## STA-2: Address checkboxes

**Change.** **Include sub-units** and **Use XY** are disabled when the form opens and are enabled only when the address picker returns a selection. **All Places** unticks and disables them again.

Before this change, a box ticked before clicking All Places stayed ticked, and the query sent addrUseXY: true or includeSubUnits: true with no addresses. The back end ignored the flags because no address filter was applied, so results were unaffected; only the display was misleading.

The labels of disabled checkboxes are greyed by the CSS rule described in CSS-1. This also greys the **KML** label until a query returns results.

## STA-3: Address labels for multiple selections

**Change.** handleAddressSelection now builds the address labels from the picker's filter string. The picker returns either a pinyin filter or a Chinese filter, never both.

| Selection | Pinyin filter used | Chinese filter used |
|---|---|---|
| All filtered results | &lt;filter&gt; [All Filtered] / [全部所濾] | [All Filtered] / &lt;filter&gt; [全部所濾] |
| Several addresses | &lt;filter&gt; [Multi-select] / [多選] | [Multi-select] / &lt;filter&gt; [多選] |
| One address | its name / its Chinese name | its name / its Chinese name |

The Texts form uses the same wording and spacing (TXT-2).

**Note.** The address-picker label proposal of 2026-10-06 is still waiting for a steering committee decision. If the committee chooses the associations-picker style, these labels will be built by the picker instead.

## TXT-1: Source-only options apply only to Biographical Sources

**Change (front end).**

- The **Main source only** and **Self-biography only** checkboxes were moved directly under the **Biographical Sources** radio button.
- onQueryModeChange() enables them only when Biographical Sources is selected. Selecting **Text Roles** or **Both** disables and unticks them. Both is the default mode, so the checkboxes start disabled.

**Change (back end).** handleQuery in texts_form_backend.go clears the two flags unless the query mode is source, so the server enforces the same rule as the page:

```
if params.QueryMode != "source" {
    params.MainSourceOnly, params.SelfBioOnly = false, false
}
```

The flags are used only in runSourceQuery, so no other code was affected.

**For the user's guide.** With **Both** selected, biographical-source records are not limited to main sources or self-biographies. The Main Source and SelfBio columns still show each record's flags.

## TXT-2: Address checkboxes and labels on the Texts form

- clearAddress() now unticks **Include sub-units** and **Use XY** as well as disabling them, matching STA-2.
- The All Filtered and Multi-select labels now have a space between the filter string and the bracket, matching STA-3.

## TXT-3: “Both” label translatable

The **Both** label (lblBoth) now has an ID, a both key in the English, Traditional and Simplified translation blocks, and a line in setLanguage. Previously it always read "Both / 两者", with the simplified 两 even in Traditional mode.

## TXT-4: Text picker labels and hover text

**Change.** The texts picker (texts_picker.html) builds the label it returns to the form. Before this change, selecting every text under a node returned the bare node name. Any other multiple selection returned Multi-Select / 多選, whether or not a search had been used. The new rules, in priority order:

| Selection | English (desc) | Chinese (descChn) |
|---|---|---|
| Exactly one text | its title | its Chinese title |
| Search active, every result selected | Srch: &lt;term&gt; [All] | 搜尋: &lt;term&gt; [全部] |
| Search active, some results selected | Srch: &lt;term&gt; [Selected] | 搜尋: &lt;term&gt; [多選] |
| No search, "(All Texts)", every text selected | All | 全部 |
| No search, "(All Texts)", some texts selected | [Selected] | [多選] |
| No search, a tree node, every text selected | &lt;node&gt; [All] | &lt;節點&gt; [全部] |
| No search, a tree node, some texts selected | &lt;node&gt; [Selected] | &lt;節點&gt; [多選] |

"Selected" and 全部 were chosen over "Multi-select" and 所有的 to keep the labels short.

**Search terms.**

- The search runs in the picker over the list it has loaded; there is no server search route.
- The picker now records the terms applied with Find or Enter (appliedEng, appliedChn). The label uses those terms, not whatever is typed in the boxes when Select is clicked.
- When only one search box was used, its term appears in both labels, for example Srch: shi [All] / 搜尋: shi [全部]. When both were used, each label shows its own term.
- With a search, [All] means every text in the search results is selected. Without a search, it means every text under the node is selected.
- A new function, clearSearch(), empties both boxes and the applied terms. It runs whenever a tree node or "(All Texts)" is clicked, so a node selection never gets a Srch: label.
- Clearing the boxes and pressing Find also ends the search, because the applied terms are then empty.
- The search terms are not passed to the form. The callback still returns { codes, desc, descChn }, so textsPickerCallback needed no change to its interface.

**Select All button.** renderList now resets the button to "Select All" whenever the list is redrawn. Previously, a Find after Select All could leave it reading "De-select All" over a list with nothing selected. The resets in the two tree-click handlers were removed because renderList now does this.

**Hover text (form).** In the Texts form's index.html, a new helper, setTextLabel(id, label), sets both the value and the title of txt-eng and txt-chn. textsPickerCallback and clearTexts() use it. Long labels can be read in full by hovering, and **All** clears the hover text.

**Comments corrected.** Two comments in the picker said that /api/texts/texts-by-category prefix-matches only category IDs of length 2 and 4, so that 5-character nodes returned nothing. handleGetTextsByCategory now prefix-matches at any length, and the comments now say so. A comment in ensureTextsLoaded that referred to the old Multi-Select label was also updated.

**Not changed.** No back-end change was needed.

**For the user's guide.**

- The text boxes show [All] when every text under the chosen node, or every search result, was selected, and [Selected] when only some were.
- A label starting with Srch: / 搜尋: means the selection came from a search.
- Hover over either box to see a label that is too long for it.

## CSS-1: Disabled-checkbox label rule consolidated

The rule greying the label of a disabled checkbox had been added separately to the Status, Texts, Association Pairs, Networks and Places sections of cbdb_styles.css. It is now one global rule in §5 (Filter rows and form inputs):

```
input[type="checkbox"]:disabled + label {
  color:  #aaa;
  cursor: default;
}
```

The five page-scoped copies were removed. The rule applies wherever a &lt;label&gt; directly follows its checkbox. Labels that wrap their checkbox, such as the Networks association-type grid, are not affected, as before.

This closes the NET-6 open item in the 2026-10-10 report.

## Correction to an earlier report

**PLC-4 (2026-10-14).** That report recorded changing the Places form's Chinese header from 指數地址 to 索引地址, on the grounds that 指數 means "index" only in the mathematical sense. That was wrong: **指數地址** is the correct term, and 索引地址 is to be reverted wherever it was introduced.

## Open items

- **ASCII Neo4j branch in Texts.** handleExportNeo4j and buildTextsNeo4jFiles keep their ASCII branches in case the option is wanted again (compare PLC-6 on Places). The page never sends encoding, so the branch is unreachable. Add a comment saying it is kept deliberately. The Encoding field of TextExportParams (GIS export) is not read.
- **Stale comments.** The comments above handleExportResults in both files describe the output files as .csv; they are written as .tsv.
- **Chinese terms.** Revert 索引地址 to 指數地址 in the HTML files (in progress). Decide whether "index year" should also be 指數年份 rather than 索引年份, which several forms use.
- **Column headers on Status.** The Status tab labels the index address "Index Place" and the People tab "Place".
- **Picker label consistency.** The texts picker now uses Srch: … [All] / 搜尋: … [全部], with square brackets and a space after the colon. The associations picker uses Search: … (All) / 搜尋:…(全部), and the address-picker plan of 2026-10-06 is still open. Review the associations picker and decide whether all pickers should share one style.
